title: LTS-aware upgrade orchestrator and gated migration plan
creator: Maya Patel
description: Deliver an orchestrator and operational plan that performs LTS-aware upgrades with gated progressive delivery. The system must coordinate version pins for LTS channels, stage traffic ramps, execute in-place schema/compatibility preflights, and run automated/observable canaries with deterministic rollback triggers. This ticket covers the orchestration engine design, controller implementation, migration hook API, and an initial console surface for scheduling LTS upgrades.
background: We currently have multiple rollout primitives (canaries, percent ramps, feature flags) but no single LTS-aware workflow that prevents accidental promotion across LTS boundaries or enforces migration prechecks. Teams running Private and Dedicated customers need predictable LTS upgrade behavior and safe migration tooling that ties into canary gates and automatic rollback logic.
goals: 1) Provide an LTS upgrade workflow that enforces channel pinning and migration windows. 2) Integrate canary and % ramping policies with automatic health-evaluated hold/rollback. 3) Expose a scheduling and audit surface in Console. 4) Offer a migration hook API for DB/schema compatibility checks.
proposal: Build an Upgrade Orchestrator service that consumes 'UpgradePlans'. An UpgradePlan includes target version, LTS-channel metadata, ramp schedule (percent steps, durations), health signal thresholds (p95 latency, error-rate, correctness smoke tests), and migration hooks. The controller will run a dry-run simulator in staging, execute preflight hooks, apply the plan across cohorts defined by LTS channel, monitor telemetry hooks, and automatically pause or rollback based on composite health scoring. Rollback policies are configurable per plan and default to conservative thresholds for LTS channels.
acceptance_criteria: Controller executes percent-based ramps with configurable step sizes and durations
Preflight migration hook API defined and used by one internal migration job
Canary runs evaluate a composite health score (latency, errors, smoke tests) and trigger automatic rollback when thresholds breached
Console surface allows scheduling an LTS upgrade with audit log entries
End-to-end test simulating a bad canary results in auto-rollback in staging
tasks: RFC + API contract for UpgradePlan and migration hooks
Implement controller core: scheduler, executor, health evaluator
Integrate existing rollout engine (percent ramps + feature flags) with LTS semantics
Add migration-hook adapter and sample DB compatibility check
Console UI: schedule wizard and audit timeline
E2E tests: dry-run simulator, staging rollout that exercises rollback
Docs: runbook, operator guide, and migration checklist
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting with Release Eng, Platform, and DB teams. Identified DB migration concern for minor->major upgrades.
2026-02-22: Spike completed on health evaluation: composite score will weight p95 latency (50%), error-rate (30%), smoke-test pass-rate (20%).
2026-03-02: RFC posted for UpgradePlan API (link in related_links). Feedback asked to add a 'hold on low-traffic' option for private customers.
2026-03-08: Architecture review: decided to reuse existing percent-ramp executor and add an LTS guard layer that blocks automatic promotion across major LTS boundaries unless explicit opt-in.
2026-03-10: PoC controller can run a two-step ramp in staging and invoke a migration hook; found flakiness in smoke-test runner—investigating.
decisions: Use percent-based ramps with adaptive backoff: if a step breaches threshold, reduce next step size by 50% and extend duration
Default rollback behavior for LTS channels is immediate revert to previous version; non-LTS (canary) can optionally pause instead
Require explicit operator confirmation for cross-major upgrades from LTS channel unless admin flag set
Migration hooks will be synchronous preflight checks before first percent step; long-running hooks run asynchronously but must report success within configurable timeout
risks: Slow or flaky migration hooks can block upgrades and create operational toil
Incorrect health scoring weights could produce false positives/negatives causing unnecessary rollbacks or undetected regressions
Console scheduling misuse could cause accidental cross-LTS promotions if guardrail UI is unclear
Interop with customer-managed private deployments (air-gapped) will require additional installers or manual steps
